tools.name: ping
tools.description: Smoke-test tool. Returns pong plus the authenticated caller's uid, tenant, and auth method. No PHI. No side effects.

tools.name: get_agency_profile
tools.description: Returns the authenticated provider's agency: id, name, slug, plan, and the caller's role. Use this first when building a vendor dashboard.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: Lists this LovedOne Soft agency's clients (agency-context loved ones). Includes whether each client is linked to a LovedOne family inbox. Does not return other agencies' clients or family-member emails.

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: Returns one client owned by this agency, plus recent visits/notes. Rejected if the client belongs to another agency.

tools.name: list_visits
tools.description: Lists LovedOne Soft visit/note events for this agency, optionally for one client. Notes may contain health information logged by staff.

tools.name: add_visit_note
tools.description: Logs a note on an agency client. If the client is linked to a LovedOne family inbox, a copy is posted there so siblings see it. This is a write. Notes may be health-related — only record what the family has asked you to share.

tools.name: schedule_visit
tools.description: Creates a scheduled visit for an agency client (agency_events type scheduled, status scheduled). Pass scheduledFor as an ISO-8601 datetime or Unix milliseconds. The visit appears in list_visits. This is a write. Notes may be health-related.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Lists invoices this agency issued to families (amounts, status, assignment). LovedOne does not move money — these are ledger records. Payment handles on the invoice are contact pointers, not credentials.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "list_invoices" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "v1" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_clients · Private data: add_visit_note, list_invoices · Public sink: add_visit_note.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_clients · Private data: add_visit_note, list_invoices · Public sink: add_visit_note

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
